user.title: Noxcast
user.description: Weather comes from Open-Meteo (free for non-commercial use, no key). Optionally add battery sensors used to detect curtailment. Add your PV arrays afterwards.

data.grid_invert: Grid sensor counts export as positive
data.feed_in: Surplus is fed into the grid

data_description.soc_sensors: Hours with a full battery are excluded from learning, because output may be curtailed.
data_description.soc_full_pct: State of charge from which curtailment is assumed.
data_description.house_load: Optional. Enables the load forecast: power of the whole house (W or kW, measurement).
data_description.day_type_entity: Optional: an entity whose state at noon is the day type, e.g. the Workday binary sensor (a holiday then counts as weekend) or an input_select such as home office / office / holiday. Profiles are learned per state.
data_description.grid_power: Optional. Power at the grid connection (W or kW, measurement), positive = import. Shows measured grid energy in the day view instead of a derived one.
data_description.grid_invert: Switch on if the grid sensor is positive while feeding in.
data_description.feed_in: Turn on if surplus power may go to the grid. Otherwise the day card counts surplus with full batteries as unused (zero export).
data_description.forecast_days: Days the forecast covers, today included (2 to 7). Further ahead the weather forecast says little about the yield.

user.title: PV array
user.description: Modules whose power is measured together (e.g. one MPPT input). Several power sensors are summed. Modules facing different directions: enter the first orientation here and the others under further orientations.

data_description.azimuth: Compass direction the modules face: 90° east, 180° south, 270° west.
data_description.peak_power: Sum of module nameplate power. With further orientations: only the modules of this first orientation.
data_description.mounting: How the modules are mounted sets how much they heat up in the sun: free behind (balcony, rack) about 30 K, parallel on a tiled roof about 50 K, integrated into the roof about 60 K.

orientation_2.name: Further orientation 2
orientation_2.description: Only for modules on the same power sensors that face another way (e.g. east and west on one input). Tilt, azimuth and the peak power of these modules; leave empty if not needed.

data_description.peak_power: Sum of module nameplate power of this orientation.
Sum of module nameplate power of this orientation.
Sum of module nameplate power of this orientation.

data_description.valid_since: Ignore older history, e.g. after moving or re-orienting the modules.
data_description.temp_coeff: Pmax temperature coefficient from the module datasheet, e.g. -0.26. Recommended. Empty = typical value (-0.35); learned only with the satellite filter.
data_description.heating: Own value instead of the mounting: how much the cells heat above the air at 1000 W/m². Empty = from the mounting.

user.title: Consumer
user.description: A device with its own sensor. Its power is taken out of the base load and forecast on its own. Next step: the fields for its timing.

data_description.power_sensor: Power of the device (W). Either this or an energy sensor.
data_description.energy_sensor: Instead of power: energy in kWh (meter or per program, total/total_increasing).
data_description.timing: Fixed: runs regardless of surplus and is part of the load forecast. Flexible: its moment should follow the surplus, so it only counts while it runs.

reconfigure.title: Consumer
reconfigure.description: A device with its own sensor. Its power is taken out of the base load and forecast on its own. Next step: the fields for its timing.

data_description.power_sensor: Power of the device (W). Either this or an energy sensor.
data_description.energy_sensor: Instead of power: energy in kWh (meter or per program, total/total_increasing).
data_description.timing: Fixed: runs regardless of surplus and is part of the load forecast. Flexible: its moment should follow the surplus, so it only counts while it runs.

fixed.title: {name}: fixed
fixed.description: Runs regardless of the surplus and is part of the load forecast.

data_description.kind: Profile: median per hour (like base load). Program: runs with an end, learned start times and runs per day (dishwasher). Session: on, then open-ended (PC, TV). Regulated: follows the outside temperature (heat pump, air conditioning).
data_description.remaining_time: Optional: remaining time of the device. A running program then counts until its end.
data_description.elapsed_time: Optional: time the program has run. With the energy sensor it gives the power of the running program.

flexible.title: {name}: flexible
flexible.description: You choose when it runs; Noxcast suggests the window. Empty values are learned from the history.

data_description.run_power: Power of a typical run. Empty = learned from its history.
data_description.run_minutes: Duration of a typical run. Empty = learned from its history.
data_description.start_share: The sensor “start now” turns on when a run started now gets at least this share from surplus and about as much as the best window still to come today. Empty = 70 %.
data_description.remaining_time: Optional: remaining time of the device. A running program then counts until its end.
data_description.elapsed_time: Optional: time the program has run. With the energy sensor it gives the power of the running program.

user.title: Battery
user.description: Battery for the surplus simulation (needs the house load). Several batteries are simulated as one storage.

data_description.coupling: DC: the battery sits behind the PV inverter's DC side (losses about 5 %). AC: own inverter (about 10 %).

limits.name: Limits
limits.description: Charge and discharge limits. Defaults: 0–100 %, no reserve.

data_description.max_soc_entity: Optional: the current charge limit from the device; it takes precedence over the number.
data_description.min_soc_entity: Optional: the current discharge limit from the device.
data_description.reserve: Percent points above the lower limit where discharging stops in practice, e.g. a feed-in stop rule.

power.name: Power
power.description: Power sensor, efficiency and power limits. All optional.

data_description.battery_power: Optional. Power of the battery (W or kW), positive = charging. The Noxcast card shows it in the power flow.
data_description.battery_power_invert: Switch on if the power sensor is positive while discharging.
data_description.efficiency: Empty = default of the coupling. Inverter losses are already in the measured values.
data_description.max_charge_w: Empty = no limit. Above it, surplus is fed in although the battery still has room.

inverter.name: Shared inverter
inverter.description: Only for a battery on the same inverter as a PV array (balcony systems).

data.array: PV array behind the same inverter

data_description.array: Optional: the PV array on the same inverter as this battery. Its PV counts against the output limit.
data_description.output_limit_w: Optional, for balcony systems: what the inverter may feed in at most (e.g. 800 W), for the battery and its PV array together. PV above it can only charge the battery.

init.title: Weather and learning sources
init.description: Weather models for the forecast and archives used when learning from history. Open-Meteo is the default and needs no key; its free API is for non-commercial use.

data_description.weather_models: Open-Meteo models, averaged hour by hour. Default ICON + ECMWF IFS: in a day-ahead test over ten months their mean beat every single model. With several models each one is also archived on its own, so the accuracy panel can compare them. "Compare weather models" in the accuracy panel shows which models suit your installation.
data_description.archive_temperature: Needed to learn the temperature loss. Without it, efficiency absorbs the average temperature.
data_description.satellite: Uses satellite irradiance to select clear hours for learning. Optional; quality varies by region.
data_description.api_key: Only for commercial or self-hosted access.

error.archive_failed: The archive could not be reached or returned an error.

error.model_unknown: Open-Meteo returned no data for these models.

no_arrays.title: Noxcast has no PV array yet
no_arrays.description: Noxcast forecasts nothing until it knows at least one PV array. Add one under Settings → Devices & services → Noxcast → ⋮ → *Add PV array*: the modules measured together (usually one MPPT input) with their power sensor, tilt, azimuth and peak power. Noxcast then learns it from the history right away.

missing_sensors.title: Noxcast is missing sensors
missing_sensors.description:
These entities are configured in Noxcast but do not exist: {sensors}.

They were probably renamed or removed. Select the new entities in the PV array, consumer or battery that uses them (Settings → Devices & services → Noxcast).

weather_unavailable.title: Noxcast gets no weather forecast
weather_unavailable.description: Open-Meteo could not be reached for more than a day, so Noxcast cannot update its forecast. Check the internet connection of Home Assistant. If you changed the weather models in the options, one of them may no longer be offered. The forecast sensors become unavailable a few hours after the last update.

array_check.title: PV array {name}: configuration does not fit the measurements
array_check.description: The measurements of **{name}** do not fit its configuration: peak power, tilt, azimuth or the power sensor may be wrong. In the Noxcast panel under *Learned*, the array shows what to check. Learned shade and efficiency stay questionable until it fits. After a correction, this report goes away with the next learning run (at night, or *Learn again now* in the panel).
